He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale Bulldogs]]. He plays the [[shooting guard]] position. Oni was named [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]] in 2019 and was a three-time All-Ivy League selection. Oni, who is of Nigerian descent, grew up in [[Northridge, Los Angeles]] and began playing high school basketball at [[Viewpoint School]], where he was named the divisional player of the year. He was lightly recruited at Viewpoint and committed to [[Williams College]] of the [[NCAA Division III]]. After drawing more interest as a senior at Viewpoint, he committed to Yale, but admissions rules forced him to play an additional season of prep basketball at [[Suffield Academy]] before college. ==Early life== Oni was born to Nigerian parents Opeyemi and Oludotun Oni. His father is a professor at the [[University of Phoenix]] and an engineer. Oni began playing basketball at age two with a toy hoop and joined a [[YMCA]] league with his older sister at age five.{{cite web |last1=Kent |first1=Richard |title=Q&A with Oludotun Oni, father of Miye Oni |url=http://ivyhoopsonline.com/2019/03/01/qa-with-oludotun-oni-father-of-miye-oni/ |publisher=Ivy Hoops Online |access-date=March 12, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190305082051/http://ivyhoopsonline.com/2019/03/01/qa-with-oludotun-oni-father-of-miye-oni/ |archive-date=March 5, 2019 |url-status=live }} From a young age, he had aspirations to play in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and admired [[Kobe Bryant]] of the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |last1=Belli |first1=Brita |title=Heading into "Ivy Madness," all eyes on NBA prospect Miye Oni |url=https://news.yale.edu/2019/03/14/heading-ivy-madness-all-eyes-nba-prospect-miye-oni |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=March 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706034306/https://news.yale.edu/2019/03/14/heading-ivy-madness-all-eyes-nba-prospect-miye-oni |archive-date=July 6, 2019 |url-status=live }} In addition to basketball, he played [[American football|football]], mainly as a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] and [[wide receiver]], and [[baseball]]. ==High school career== Oni began his freshman year at [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Chatsworth, California]], but transferred to enroll and play basketball at [[Viewpoint School]] in [[Calabasas, California]] before the season started. He played for the [[junior varsity team]] in his freshman season, when he stood {{convert|5|ft|9|in|m|2}} and weighed {{convert|140|lbs|kg|0}}.{{cite web |last1=Fattal |first1=Tarek |title=Former Viewpoint basketball player Miye Oni emerging as first-round NBA prospect |url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/05/former-viewpoint-basketball-player-miye-oni-emerging-as-first-round-nba-prospect/ |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |access-date=March 12, 2019 |date=January 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202221258/https://www.dailynews.com/2019/01/05/former-viewpoint-basketball-player-miye-oni-emerging-as-first-round-nba-prospect/ |archive-date=February 2, 2019 |url-status=live }} He did not play on the school's basketball team as a sophomore to focus on his education. As a junior, Oni suffered a knee injury that sidelined him for most of the season.{{cite web |last1=Jacobs |first1=Jeff |title=The NBA may be in his future, but Miye Oni is relishing a special season at Yale |url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/jeffjacobs/article/Jeff-Jacobs-The-NBA-may-be-in-his-future-but-13527849.php |website=[[Connecticut Post]] |access-date=March 12, 2019 |date=January 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190203022711/https://www.ctpost.com/sports/jeffjacobs/article/Jeff-Jacobs-The-NBA-may-be-in-his-future-but-13527849.php |archive-date=February 3, 2019 |url-status=live }} The injury hindered his [[college recruiting]] because he did not have film to show college coaches before his senior year. Oni stood {{convert|6|ft|4|in|m|2}} and weighed {{convert|180|lbs|kg|0}} by the time he was a senior. He had a breakout final season for Viewpoint, averaging 18 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 assists and being named [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) Division 5AA player of the year.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/bios/oni_miye_npi2 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 12, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190313123553/http://yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2017-18/bios/oni_miye_npi2 |archive-date=March 13, 2019 |url-status=live }} At Viewpoint, Oni did not draw interest from [[NCAA Division I]] basketball programs and was only recruited by [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] school [[Williams College]], where he committed in the fall of his senior year of high school. However, Williams did not offer enough [[student financial aid (United States)|financial aid]] for his family to meet the cost of attendance. During his senior season at Viewpoint, Oni attracted attention from [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball|Yale]] assistant coach Matt Kingsley. After watching his highlight video in the spring of 2015, Yale head coach [[James Jones (basketball, born 1964)|James Jones]] offered him, and Oni committed to play for the team on July 1, 2015.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni |url=http://www.espn.com/collegskee-sports/batball/recruiting/player/_/id/213447/miye-oni |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 13, 2019}} However, since Yale admissions were closed, he spent his next season playing for [[Suffield Academy]], a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Suffield, Connecticut]], located near [[Yale University]]. With Suffield, Oni averaged 17 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists and earned [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]] (NEPSAC) Class A player of the year distinction. On February 5, 2016, he scored 52 points with 11 three-pointers versus [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] at the National Prep School Invitational, breaking his school record and [[Shabazz Napier]]'s tournament record.{{cite web |last1=Evans |first1=Corey |title=NPSI Day One: Miye Oni scorches the nets |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201602/npsi-day-one-miye-oni-scorches-nets |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=March 14, 2019 |date=February 5, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628014212/http://www.hoopseen.com/news/general/201602/npsi-day-one-miye-oni-scorches-nets |archive-date=June 28, 2017 |url-status=live }} Oni was named most outstanding player of the event. |url=https://www.mcdonaldsallamerican.com/content/aag/en/MediaCenter/2016/2016-game-materials/2016-Nominee-List/_jcr_content/featuredcontent/everything/file.res/2016%20Nominee%20List%20%28Boys_Girls%29%20Final%281%29.pdf |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |url-status=live }} ==College career== ===Freshman season=== Oni made his debut for Yale on November 13, 2016, recording a team-high 24 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 assists averaged 15.1 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game, leading Yale in all three categories. He tied the school record for three-pointers attempted in a single season, with 184.{{cite web |title=Team & Individual Records |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2011-12/files/records_web.pdf |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 19, 2019 three-time Ivy League Player of the Week, unanimous first-team All-Ivy League pick, and [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC) District 13 second-team selection. ===Junior season=== [[File:Miye Oni (cropped 2).jpg|thumb|Oni (right) skies for a block in December 2018.]] Oni made his junior season debut on November 9, 2018, scoring 16 points in a 76–59 win over [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] at the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] China Game held in [[Shanghai]].{{cite web |title=Oni, Swain Pace Yale With 16 Points |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/201811105b3j5v |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=November 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190319224546/http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/201811105b3j5v |archive-date=March 19, 2019 |url-status=live }} On November 21, he posted his first double-double of the season, leading his team with 18 points and 10 rebounds in a 79–70 loss to Vermont.{{cite web |title=Vermont Edges Yale 79-70 |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20181121varlkf |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=November 21, 2018 Oni scored 29 points and was named game MVP in a 77–73 victory over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]] at the Hoophall Miami Invitational.{{cite web |title=Miye Oni leads Yale's 2nd-half rally past Miami, 77-73 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/12/01/miye-oni-leads-yales-2nd-half-rally-past-miami-77-73/38655555/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=December 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181203062522/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/12/01/miye-oni-leads-yales-2nd-half-rally-past-miami-77-73/38655555/ |archive-date=December 3, 2018 |url-status=live }}{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 29 Points, Named Game MVP |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20181201xdue15 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=December 1, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190211145232/http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20181201xdue15 |archive-date=February 11, 2019 |url-status=live }} He erupted for 31 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 assists, leading his team in each category, on February 2, 2019, in an 89–68 win over Dartmouth. Oni was the first Yale player to record a 30-point game since Anthony Dallier in 2017.{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 31, Bulldogs Rout Dartmouth |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190202y7ihj9 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 19, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221035433/http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190202y7ihj9 |archive-date=February 21, 2019 |url-status=live }} In his next game, a 74–60 victory over [[Princeton Tigers men's basketball|Princeton]], he posted a career-high 35 points, 12 rebounds, and 3 blocks. Oni scored the most single-game points in school history since [[Greg Mangano]] in 2012.{{cite web |title=Oni Scores 35 As Bulldogs Knock Off Princeton 74-60 |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190208wgxb3j |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190319225250/http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190208wgxb3j |archive-date=March 19, 2019 |url-status=live }} He delivered another strong performance on March 1, when he scored 30 points—shooting 9-of-11 from the field—to help Yale defeat [[Cornell Big Red men's basketball|Cornell]], 88–65, and clinch a spot in the [[2019 Ivy League men's basketball tournament|2019 Ivy league tournament]].{{cite web |title=Bulldogs Clinch Spot In IvyMadness, Hammer Cornell 88-65 |work=Yale |url=http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190301ws51j9 |publisher=[[Yale University]] |access-date=March 19, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324175423/http://www.yalebulldogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/2018-19/releases/20190301ws51j9 |archive-date=March 24, 2019 |url-status=live }} By the end of the regular season, Oni was averaging a team-best 17.4 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 3.6 assists per game. He was named [[Ivy League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ivy League Player of the Year]], becoming the third Yale player to win the award.{{cite web |last1=Fuller |first1=Jim |title=Yale's Miye Oni named Ivy League Player of the Year |url=https://www.nhregister.com/colleges/article/Yale-s-Miye-Oni-named-Ivy-League-Player-of-the-13683367.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |access-date=March 19, 2019 |date=March 12, 2019}} In his junior season, Oni frequently attracted attention from NBA scouts, who visited all of his games to see him play.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Don |title=For Yale's Miye Oni, the story just keeps getting better |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/college/hc-sp-amore-column-yale-miye-oni-20190318-20190318-ggkk7v3hsng7pd5mqe46c32nra-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=March 18, 2019 |date=March 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322134522/https://www.courant.com/sports/college/hc-sp-amore-column-yale-miye-oni-20190318-20190318-ggkk7v3hsng7pd5mqe46c32nra-story.html |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |url-status=live }} He was considered a top-50 prospect for the [[2019 NBA draft]] and became the first Ivy League player to be drafted since 1995. In December 2018, [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] head coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] predicted that he would be a first-round pick. ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2019–2022)=== On June 20, 2019, Oni was selected as the 58th pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. His draft rights were traded to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/draft-poole-paschall-20190621|title=Warriors Select Jordan Poole and Eric Paschall in 2019 NBA Draft|date=June 21, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 21, 2019|quote=The Warriors selected Yale University's Miye Oni with the 58th overall pick in the second round before completing a trade with Utah to send Oni's draft rights to the Jazz in exchange for cash considerations.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621192523/https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/draft-poole-paschall-20190621|archive-date=June 21, 2019|url-status=live}} With the selection, Oni became the first [[Ivy League]] men's basketball player picked in the NBA draft since [[Jerome Allen (basketball)|Jerome Allen]] in 1995 and the first [[Yale Bulldogs men's basketball]] player picked since [[Chris Dudley]] in 1987.{{cite web |last1=McCormack |first1=William |last2=Zillo |first2=Cristofer |title=Miye Oni selected by Golden State, traded to Utah Jazz with 58th pick in 2019 NBA draft |url=https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2019/06/21/golden-state-selects-miye-oni-20-with-58th-pick-in-2019-nba-draft/ |website=[[Yale Daily News]] |access-date=June 21, 2019 |date=June 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621162040/https://yaledailynews.com/blog/2019/06/21/golden-state-selects-miye-oni-20-with-58th-pick-in-2019-nba-draft/ |archive-date=June 21, 2019 |url-status=live }} On July 15, 2019, the [[Utah Jazz]] signed Oni.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-miye-oni|title=Utah Jazz sign Miye Oni|date=July 15, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715181912/https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-miye-oni|archive-date=July 15, 2019|url-status=live}} He was assigned to the [[Salt Lake City Stars]] for the start of the [[NBA G League]] season. He scored a season-high 28 points for the Stars in a win over the [[Memphis Hustle]] on January 10, 2020.{{cite news |title=Jazz's Miye Oni: Leads squad with 28 points Friday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-miye-oni-leads-squad-with-28-points-friday/ |access-date=January 11, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 11, 2020}} The 2019-2020 Salt Lake City Stars ended up breaking the NBA G League record for most consecutive wins with 14 and finished the season with the best record. Oni averaged 12.7 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 4 assists in all contests. Later in his rookie season, Oni began to get looked on to play for the Jazz, as injuries to [[Bojan Bogdanovic]] left a hole in the team heading into the NBA Bubble. On August 7, 2020, Oni recorded his first start and scored his NBA career high 14 points and 7 rebounds for the Jazz in a loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite news |title=Jazz rookies show spirit, potential in loss to Spurs|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2020/8/7/21358529/utah-jazz-san-antonio-spurs-nba-bubble-rayjon-tucker-miye-oni-tony-bradley-jarrell-brantley?_amp=true|access-date=August 7, 2020 |work=[[Deseret News]] |date=August 7, 2020}} In his second year with the Jazz, Oni became a rotation regular, often filling in for injuries at the guard position. Oni appeared in 54 of the 72 regular season games, and the Jazz finished the season with a league best 52–20 record and the top seed in the Western Conference.{{cite news |title= Jazz Clinch West's No. 1 Seed, Home-Court Advantage in 2021 NBA Playoffs|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10002869-jazz-clinch-wests-no-1-seed-home-court-advantage-in-2021-nba-playoffs |access-date=May 17, 2021 |work=[[Bleacher Report]] |date=May 17, 2021}} Oni was called upon to play key minutes for the Jazz in the 2022 NBA Playoffs, notably matching up with [[Paul George]] of the Los Angeles Clippers. In his third season with the Jazz, new additions to the roster led to Oni falling out of the rotation. On January 4, 2022, Oni was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] along with a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for cash considerations.{{Cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Miye Oni|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-oni-220104|access-date=January 4, 2022|website=Oklahoma City Thunder}} Three days later, he was waived.{{Cite web|title=Thunder Waives Oni|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/oni-220107|access-date=January 10, 2022|website=NBA}} On February 4, 2022, Oni signed a 10-day hardship contract with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{Cite web|title=Pelicans sign Cheatham and Oni to 10-day contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-zylan-cheatham-miye-oni-10-day-contracts|access-date=February 4, 2022|website=NBA}} Oni joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]],{{Cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612742/mavericks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===London Lions (2022–2023)=== On November 16, 2022, Oni signed with [[London Lions (basketball)|London Lions]] of the [[British Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Miye Oni joins the London Lions for the rest of the season|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1420121/miye-oni-london-lions-eurocup/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}} He became the 4th former NBA draft pick to sign with the Lions in 2022, joining [[Sam Dekker]], [[Kosta Koufos]], and [[Tomislav Zubčić]]. In their first season in the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]], the Lions became the first British club in history to clinch a berth in the EuroCup Playoffs.{{cite web|title=London locks up playoff spot by beating Hamburg | EuroCup|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/london-locks-up-playoff-spot-by-beating-hamburg/|website=EuroleagueBasketball.net|date=February 8, play for the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team]] at the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] in [[Tokyo]] due to his mother being born there. He saw significant minutes and made the go-ahead three point field goal when Nigeria upset the [[United States men's national basketball team]] in an exhibition game prior to the start of the Games. Oni then appeared in all three games in Tokyo, starting two of the three and averaging 21.8 minutes which was second on the team.
